subject: Accounting
title: Preserving Digital Evidence
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Preserving Digital Evidence.

hook.text: One wrong click can alter a file's metadata—and that can get crucial evidence thrown out of court.

buildup.text: Digital evidence must be collected, copied, and stored using forensically sound methods.

discovery.text: Chain of custody documentation tracks who handled the evidence, when, and what was done with it.

twist.text: A bit-for-bit copy (forensic image) preserves everything—including deleted files and hidden partitions.

climax.text: Without proper preservation, even the strongest evidence can be challenged and excluded at trial.

punchline.text: Find the evidence. Then protect it like it's made of glass.

quiz.question: Why is chain of custody important for digital evidence?
options: It proves the evidence hasn't been tampered with
It reduces the cost of forensic analysis

details.summary: Preserving digital evidence ensures that electronic records—files, emails, databases, and device data—remain intact, unaltered, and admissible in court. This topic covers chain of custody, forensic imaging, and the legal requirements for handling digital evidence.
details.whyItMatters: Digital evidence that isn't properly preserved can be challenged as tampered or unreliable, potentially destroying an otherwise strong case. Proper preservation is non-negotiable in forensic investigations.
takeaways: Forensic imaging creates a bit-for-bit copy of storage media with a hash value proving integrity
Chain of custody documentation tracks who handled the evidence, when, and what they did with it
Original evidence should never be examined directly—all analysis is performed on verified copies

faq.question: How is digital evidence preserved for legal proceedings?
faq.answer: A forensic image (exact bit-for-bit copy) is created from the original media using write-blocking hardware. Hash values (digital fingerprints) verify the copy matches the original. All handling is documented in a chain of custody log. Analysis is performed only on copies, never originals.

faq.question: What happens if digital evidence is improperly preserved?
faq.answer: Improperly preserved evidence can be challenged as unreliable or tampered with, potentially being ruled inadmissible by the court. Without proper chain of custody, defense attorneys can argue evidence was modified, planted, or contaminated—undermining the entire case.
